messages:
incident-bot: PAGER -> SEV1 serving-runtime: elevated CUDA OOMs on decode-stream pools (us-west-2). Symptoms: CUDA out of memory, container exit 137, node restarts. Observed ~1200 failed streaming requests/min. Paging @alice (oncall) and runtime team.

alice: ack — I'm on it. creating incident thread here.

bob: digging in logs. early signal points to runaway generation on rdx-7b-stream after the recent model rollout. Lots of requests generating >>100k tokens; KV cache growth + decoder loop not enforcing hard cap. Example log: 
```
2026-03-15T10:12:34Z ERROR decode: cuda runtime error (2): out of memory
model=rdx-7b-stream:v2 request_id=abcd-1234 tokens_generated=248912
stack: infer->decode_loop->kv_append
```

bob: That token_count explains OOMs and container churn — kernel thrashing, OOM kills, node flaps. Also seeing client IPs with sustained open streams.

alice: immediate mitigations? what's safe to do without broad customer impact.

bob: prioritized mitigations (recommended):
1) Route streaming traffic to a safe fallback model (rdx-7b-compact) that has strict server-side caps.
2) Hot-patch model config to set max_tokens=2048 and enforce per-request streaming cap.
3) Throttle/ban offending client IPs at edge temporarily.
4) Cordon affected nodes and kill runaway containers to free GPU memory.
5) Add quick alert rule for per-request token rate.

alice: doing #1 now. @deploy-bot — can you flip a route override for streaming?

deploy-bot: route-change: applied route override: /v1/stream -> rdx-7b-compact for tag=prod-streaming :white_check_mark: (route id: r-33bc)

dana: support here — we're starting customer outreach for any 5xx spikes. Which customers should we prioritize?

bob: send to customers using the streaming endpoint and those reporting increased error rates (svc:search-chat). I can pull request ids (sample) and correlate.

bob: hotfix ready. Patch we will apply: set max_tokens and stream_chunk_size, enforce server-side hard cap. Patch command: 
```
kubectl patch configmodel rdx-7b-stream --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/max_tokens","value":2048}]'
kubectl patch configmodel rdx-7b-stream --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/stream_chunk_size","value":64}]'
```

alice: applying patch now. also cordoning node-uw2-03 and evicting pods on suspected hosts.

carlos: I'm joining the rotation, taking over on-call. I'll coordinate node ops. pulling nvidia-smi and dmesg.

carlos: found two runaway processes on node-uw2-03 with very large GPU memory allocations. PIDs: 4521, 4529. Killing them freed ~28GB each. After kill, containers restarted cleanly.

carlos: executed: 
```
docker kill 4521 && docker kill 4529
kubectl cordon node-uw2-03
kubectl drain node-uw2-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

carlos: cleared KV caches on restarted pods; observed immediate drop in cuda OOM logs.

incident-bot: Incident update: route override applied, config hotfix rolled, 6 nodes cordoned/2 drained+rebooted. Request drop rate reduced from ~1200/min -> ~5/min. Error rate back to baseline. Downgrading to P2.

dana: outreach in progress to top affected accounts. Offering 1 week credit for impacted requests. No evidence of data leakage.

bob: Root cause (preliminary): regression in recent model rollout where max_tokens was set inadvertently high (100000) combined with a missing server-side hard cap in the streaming path. This allowed a small set of clients to request runaway generations that exhausted GPU memory and filled KV cache.

bob: Follow-ups assigned:
- add server-side hard cap for streaming (2048) — high priority
- add per-request anomaly detection for token generation rate
- revert/verify model rollout validation checks in CI to prevent config drift
- add circuit-breaker at gateway for sustained token-heavy sessions

alice: thanks. Bob/Dana/Carlos please prepare artifacts for the postmortem: traces, sample requests, list of affected customers, and node dmesg. We'll run RCA 2026-03-16 10:00 UTC.

carlos: taking ownership of node remediation & preventive infra tasks. also adding a health-check that triggers when per-pod token_generation > 50k in 5m.

dana: support note: customers notified; incident ticket numbers created and linked to this thread.

alice: handing off final incident follow-ups. Good work everyone. Closing paging rotation. :thumbsup:

notes: keep this thread for the postmortem write-up. Include timeline, mitigations, and lessons learned (server-side caps, rollout validation, token-rate detection).
